answer: Each key must publish a self-assessed worth and pay a continuous tax on it; anyone may then buy it outright at the declared figure. Claiming little keeps tax trivial but caps earnable emission; claiming much invites immediate purchase, so a farm cannot look worthless and harvest real revenue. Sybils are pinned to a narrow ridge where declared value must match true value, and any profitable clone is expropriated at its quoted price. No marble monument certifies lineage; the tax enforces it. Ten thousand keys pay ten thousand taxes yet still split one honest share, like yarrow among stones.
